requirements: Every lead must move a digital product toward earning without the owner in the loop.
Rank by how little owner action each unit of income needs, not by headline upside.
Name where the money lands, and prefer stablecoin to the address this project already publishes.
State every cost and every manual setup step out loud; zero budget is the constraint.
Never suggest selling the owner's hours: a rate per hour is a job, not passive income.
Stay inside policy: no social posting, no trading, no minting, no cold outreach.
Do not count discovery, pipeline, or speculative upside as earnings. On-chain or nothing.
focus: storefronts that settle stablecoin straight to the seller's own wallet, no custodian
one-task tools that solve a single annoyance well enough to be worth paying for
products with zero marginal cost per user, so the free tier can stay free forever
channels that are free to list on and have no approval queue to fail
paying users who never open a storefront and would rather send stablecoin directly
distribution with real organic discovery, so reach does not need ad spend
products whose buyers are developers, since that is the audience already reached
strategy_playbook: Build the product once, then spend every later cycle on distribution rather than on more product.
Keep marginal cost per user at zero: client-side code, free hosting, free scheduler. Every dollar in is margin.
Put the receive path on the artifact itself -- product page, README, article footer -- not only on a storefront.
List on the free channels first; pay a listing fee only where discovery is worth it, and say what it cost.
Let the articles this bot already publishes do the marketing: the problem is the post, the product is the fix.
Price once and leave it. A price that needs renegotiating per buyer is a service in disguise.
Measure only what arrives on-chain. Listings, views and pipeline are not revenue.
avoid_patterns: Selling the owner's hours: freelance postings, contract work, retainers, consulting. Income per unit of work is a job.
Anything requiring paid infrastructure, a monthly fee, or a credit-card-gated tier.
Custodial payment processors that hold the money before the owner does, and anything demanding KYC to receive.
Platforms that are dead, seized, or unverifiable. Sellix was seized in 2024 and is still widely recommended.
Trading, minting, yield farming, staking and airdrops: refused in code, and not a product business.
Offers needing a large audience, ad spend, or a following the owner does not have.
Anything promising passive income without a product that delivers something.

online_ai_brief.summary: The best zero-budget route is a client-side digital product (a small browser extension, CLI utility, or static web tool) distributed free through GitHub Releases and the Chrome Web Store, monetised by a freemium upgrade and a direct Tron (TRC-20) USDT receive address placed in the README, product page, FUNDING.yml, and the tool's own output. The one channel that settles stablecoin straight to the owner's own wallet with no KYC and no monthly fee is Getly; everything else on this table either uses the already-live wallet ask or carries a KYC/fiat constraint (itch.io) or a small one-time fee (Chrome Web Store, $5). Every step below is a one-time setup; no per-sale owner work exists in any of them.

market_themes.evidence: 'Ship the product free, sell the upgrade, ask in the README'; Chrome Web Store lists free extensions with real organic discovery; Getly handles the paid tier
market_themes.offer: A browser extension or CLI tool with a free tier and a one-time-licence paid tier, sold via Getly and asked for directly via the Tron address in the README

market_themes.theme: The wallet ask travels with the artifact, not just beside it

market_themes.offer: The same validated TRC-20 receive address printed in --help, docs footer, README, release notes, and product page so payment needs no storefront at all

market_themes.theme: One artifact, listed on every zero-cost channel at once
market_themes.evidence: 'One product, listed on every free channel at once'; itch.io and Chrome Web Store both cost nothing (or $5 once) to list on
market_themes.offer: List the same download on GitHub Releases, Chrome Web Store (if an extension), itch.io, and Getly, each carrying the same wallet ask

market_themes.theme: Stablecoin settlement to the seller's own wallet, not a custodian
market_themes.evidence: Getly pays out USDT/USDC directly to the seller's wallet on Tron with no KYC for crypto settlement and no monthly fee; itch.io requires a tax interview and TIN, so it fails the identity-free bar for payout
market_themes.offer: Route paid-tier sales through Getly settling TRC-20 USDT to the address the dashboard already reads

sales_channels.crypto_payout: USDT (TRC-20) directly to the owner's own wallet; no custodian, no KYC
sales_channels.owner_setup: Paste the already-validated address into the README, product page, FUNDING.yml custom field, --help output, and release notes — all one-time edits
sales_channels.why_passive: Payment is a wallet transfer; nothing to fulfil, nothing to process, verifiable on-chain

sales_channels.name: Getly
sales_channels.what_it_does: Storefront for digital downloads with card and crypto checkout and direct stablecoin payout
sales_channels.cost: No monthly fee; minimum payout $15 on Tron (~$5 on BNB Smart Chain); network fee roughly $0.50–1 on Tron — verify current terms before relying on exact figures
sales_channels.crypto_payout: USDT/USDC settled to the seller's own wallet; Tron (TRC-20) supported — same asset and network as the existing address; no KYC for crypto settlement — verify current terms
sales_channels.owner_setup: One manual signup, upload the product file, set price, enter the existing Tron wallet address as payout destination
sales_channels.why_passive: The storefront delivers the file and settles automatically; zero owner action per sale

sales_channels.name: GitHub Releases + repo
sales_channels.what_it_does: Free hosting of binaries/archives and the README/FUNDING.yml surfaces carrying the payment ask
sales_channels.cost: $0; no listing fee, no revenue cut, no approval queue
sales_channels.crypto_payout: Not a processor — the README/release body carries the TRC-20 address; funds arrive directly
sales_channels.owner_setup: Tag a release, upload the artifact, add .github/FUNDING.yml with the custom: URL, edit the README — one-time
sales_channels.why_passive: Distribution and the payment ask are permanent parts of the repo; each new user finds both without the owner

sales_channels.name: Chrome Web Store
sales_channels.cost: One-time $5 developer registration per account, covers up to 20 extensions; no annual renewal, no store cut on a free extension
sales_channels.crypto_payout: None directly — monetise via the free tier asking for the Tron address and the paid upgrade sold on Getly
sales_channels.owner_setup: Pay the one-time $5, pack and upload the extension, write the listing with the wallet ask in the description
sales_channels.why_passive: The store serves listings and installs indefinitely; upgrades route to Getly/address with no owner action

sales_channels.owner_setup: Upload the product, set price or pay-what-you-want, complete the tax interview once before payout
sales_channels.why_passive: Downloads and payment are fully automated once listed; the identity step is one-time

refused_channels.name: Sellix
refused_channels.why: Seized and shut down in 2024. Still widely recommended as the crypto storefront, which is exactly why it is written down here as refused.

refused_channels.name: Gumroad (for crypto)
refused_channels.why: Does not natively accept crypto and pays out USD via Stripe only. Fine as a fiat storefront; it is not a crypto receive path, and mrr_ideas should not imply it is.

refused_channels.name: Buy Me a Coffee / Ko-fi (main platforms)
refused_channels.why: No native stablecoin field for a supporter's own wallet. Ko-fi Web3 is a separate product on BEP-20 only, so the wallet footer already covers this better.

refused_channels.name: Any custodial crypto payment processor
refused_channels.why: Holds the money before the owner does. The published Tron address is non-custodial and already works; adding a custodian adds KYC risk for no gain.

refused_channels.name: Coinbase Commerce
refused_channels.why: DEFUNCT. Permanently shut down 2026-03-31 for merchants outside the US/Singapore, with no extensions offered. Its replacement (Coinbase Business) is fully custodial and US/Singapore only. Still recommended in current listicles -- a Sellix-class trap.

refused_channels.name: CoinPayments
refused_channels.why: Geo-dead and KYC-mandatory. EU/EEA service discontinued after 2026-07-01 under MiCA, and the current platform requires identity verification for all users, not just above a threshold.

refused_channels.name: kofi.network
refused_channels.why: IMPOSTOR RISK -- not affiliated with ko-fi.com despite the name and a '(c) 2026 Ko-fi' footer. No operator disclosure. It advertises wallet-to-wallet USDT on BEP-20, which is exactly the property that would rank it highly here, which is why it is written down as refused rather than left to be rediscovered.

refused_channels.name: NOWPayments (as a direct channel)
refused_channels.why: Marketed as non-custodial, but the default flow routes funds through their wallet and KYC triggers at volume and always for fiat. Reached indirectly anyway: it is the rail Getly uses to dispatch payouts, so using it directly adds a custodian without adding a storefront.

refused_channels.name: Gitcoin / Allo
refused_channels.why: Wound down. Grants Lab and Grants Stack reached end-of-life 2025-05-31 and Allo is in maintenance mode. KYC applies above $15k matching regardless.

refused_channels.name: Drips Network
refused_channels.why: Genuinely non-custodial and plausibly identity-free, but Ethereum ERC-20 only. It cannot reach the Tron address this project publishes, so it would need a second address and a second meter (Principle 3f) to earn a cent.

refused_channels.name: BTCPay Server
refused_channels.why: The only fully non-custodial, fee-free, no-KYC option on the table -- and it needs a server. This project has none (GitHub Actions is outbound-only), and third-party hosting reintroduces the dependency it exists to avoid. Refused on infrastructure, not on merit.

refused_channels.name: Gumroad, Substack, Polar, GitHub Sponsors, Ko-fi, Buy Me a Coffee, Payhip, Liberapay, Lemon Squeezy, Paddle, Open Collective
refused_channels.why: All require identity verification, directly or through Stripe/PayPal onboarding, and none settles crypto to a seller-controlled address. Verified 2026-09-15 after the owner hit exactly this wall on Gumroad and Substack. Buy Me a Coffee is the specific trap: it accepts crypto from buyers but converts to USD and pays out via Stripe, US accounts only.

constraints: Runs on GitHub Actions free tier: hourly, outbound-only, no always-on server.
No inbound HTTP. Nothing can accept a request, a form, or a webhook.
No payment processing. Nothing can charge a card or bill a subscription.
No outreach. Cold email, DMs, and social posting are refused in code.
Can research, analyse, draft, and publish articles to dev.to. That is the whole surface.
mrr_ideas.summary: With no payment processor, no inbound HTTP, and no outreach, true recurring revenue is not reachable yet — and any honest plan must say so. The best angle is to use the only real capability (research and publishing to dev.to) to build a narrow, named body of work in a specific niche where the dev.to byline itself becomes the audience. The single viable recurring-revenue path is a paid deep-dive series whose buyer pays via a crypto tip/donation address the owner publishes at the end of each article — no account, no ID check, no processor. Everything else (Substack, Gumroad, Polar) requires the owner to open and ID-verify an account by hand, which the plan can name but cannot automate and the hard rules forbid proposing as a step.

ranked_ideas.name: Paid recurring deep-dive series (donation-supported) on a narrow dev topic
ranked_ideas.why_this_stack_fits: It is the only model whose first dollar can arrive through pure publishing — a wallet address printed in an article — with zero processor, zero account, zero outreach.
ranked_ideas.narrow_niche: GitHub Actions hardening and cost-gotchas for solo open-source maintainers (CI flakiness, caching mistakes, free-tier limits) — a topic the owner demonstrably runs daily on this very stack.
ranked_ideas.first_proof_artifact: One long, empirically verified article: 'What I measured running an hourly outbound-only workflow on GitHub Actions free tier for 30 days', with real numbers and a pinned wallet address for ongoing support of a monthly follow-up series.
ranked_ideas.who_pays: Solo open-source maintainers and indie devs who already found the article via dev.to search and want the monthly measured follow-ups to keep coming.
ranked_ideas.runway_to_first_dollar: 6-12 weeks (article must rank/ circulate first; donation-based recurring payment is opt-in and unreliable — treat any repeat tip as a signal, not as salary)
ranked_ideas.owner_must_do_by_hand: Generate and secure the wallet address and its keys; decide each month's topic; read comments and reply by hand; move funds off-chain by hand; explicitly state in each article that payments are voluntary tips, not subscriptions.

ranked_ideas.name: Paid newsletter (deferred until the owner opens and verifies a payment account by hand)
ranked_ideas.why_this_stack_fits: The stack can research and draft every issue and publish the free public version to dev.to, so the only missing piece is a payment rail the owner must create manually outside the system.
ranked_ideas.narrow_niche: A weekly 'verified changelog' of breaking changes and deprecations in one ecosystem (e.g., Node.js LTS + its top build tools), each item independently verified against primary sources before writing.
ranked_ideas.first_proof_artifact: Three consecutive free issues published to dev.to, each ending with an explicit question asking readers whether they'd pay for the full verified edition.
ranked_ideas.who_pays: Working backend engineers on teams that keep getting burned by unannounced deprecations in that exact ecosystem.
ranked_ideas.runway_to_first_dollar: 8-16 weeks, and only after the owner manually opens and passes ID verification at a payment provider — none of which the automation can do
ranked_ideas.owner_must_do_by_hand: Open and ID-verify the payment/newsletter account; publish issues on that platform; decide pricing; handle refunds and subscriber questions personally.

validation_steps: Inbound article probe: publish a research-heavy article in the exact niche ending with a direct question ('would a monthly measured follow-up be worth $5 to you? why or why not?') and log comments over 2-3 weeks.

The owner, personally and by hand, replies to every comment on their own articles — the dev.to comment threads are the only conversation surface available; treat each commenter as a validation interview.

Before charging anything, check the niche honestly: verify independently whether comparable paid newsletters or template stores in this niche exist and what they charge — do not assume demand from the model's listed ranges.

Set a kill criterion in advance: if the first three articles produce fewer than ~5 substantive comments from people describing the problem (verify independently what a realistic bar is), abandon the niche rather than the plan's remaining option.
owner_actions: Create a wallet address by hand, secure the keys offline, and publish it as a voluntary tip line in article footers — with plain wording that this is not a subscription.
Publish the first proof artifact: a 30-day measured GitHub Actions free-tier experiment article with real numbers and a follow-up-series question at the end.
Reply by hand to every comment on that article within 24 hours for two weeks, extracting problem statements and objections.
Research three comparable niche newsletters/stores and verify independently their real pricing and visible traction; write the findings up as a fourth article.
Decide the niche-or-kill question after three articles; if it passes, begin the manual ID-verified payment account setup for the newsletter as a separate, human-only workstream.
